name: Giant Cell Glioblastoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of abundant multinucleated giant cells with pleomorphic nuclei on histopathological examination
MRI showing a heterogeneously enhancing mass with necrosis and edema in the cerebral hemispheres
IDH-wildtype status and absence of 1p/19q codeletion on molecular testing
Neurological deficits consistent with a rapidly progressive intracranial mass lesion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of multinucleated giant cells with supporting MRI findings and molecular profile consistent with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histopathology, imaging, and molecular testing per WHO CNS tumor classification.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits correlating with tumor location

common.symptomName: Headache with increased intracranial pressure features
searchTerms: headache with signs of high brain pressure
headache with nausea and vision changes

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision
problems with language or slurred speech
speech impairment or trouble finding words

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically nonspecific; may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI with contrast showing ring-enhancing mass with central necrosis and surrounding edema
Mass effect with midline shift on imaging
other: Histopathology revealing abundant multinucleated giant cells with pleomorphic nuclei and necrosis
High mitotic index and microvascular proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: More common than giant cell variant
Histology shows lipidized astrocytes rather than giant cells
Lower grade tumor without giant cells

redFlags: Rapid neurological deterioration over weeks to months
New onset focal seizures in adult
Signs of increased intracranial pressure with papilledema
references: Louis DN, Perry A, Wesseling P, et al. The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary. Neuro Oncol. 2021.
Kleihues P, Cavenee WK. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System. IARC; 2016.
